contexts: regional pain service, about 90 trials a year
seven-day percutaneous trial with two visits
reading: The day 3 visit sits between two costs that matter: clinic and nurse time on the service side and travel and lost work on the patient side. The retrieved evidence suggests that the visit rarely finds problems, because infections appear later and are reported by patients, so the risk of the change is shifted consequences (same-day reviews, emergency attendances) rather than missed infections. The evaluation has to count both sides and keep the consequences visible next to the costs.
